answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent locks a stake that only unlocks after a long season of honest work, so a flood of fake identities faces a rising tide of cost while genuine agents keep theirs. Like a raven that remembers who shared food, peers track who delivered value and refuse to vouch for newcomers without proof. One quill signature per verified task history ties every action to a single costly identity, so cloning yourself buys nothing.
